:JUDGMENT:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Bhavishath in the Road Traffic Accident dated 15.11.2023.
2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 15.11.2023 at about 8.40 a.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03- JS-3267 as pillion rider ridden by his friend slowly, cautiously on correct side of the road and reached in front of Jyothi School,
near Booragamakalahalli, Srinivasapura - Chintamani road, Chintamani Taluk, at that time, respondent's Maruthi SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2856/2024 Swift Dzire car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-B-0326 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle)
came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and went to its wrong side and dashed violently against the motorcycle of the petitioner.

As a result, petitioner fell down from motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.
3.

Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Chintamani, and after first aid shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical hospital, Kolar, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

4. In pursuance of service of the notice issued to the Respondent No.1 and 2 they appeared through their Counsels and filed Objections to the claim petition.

The Respondent No.1 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2856/2024 It is submitted by the respondent No.1 that the rider of the motorcycle was tortfeasor and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the rider.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle is insured under the respondent No.2.
It is submitted that the petitioner was not having valid driving license at the time of the accident.
It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The driver of the said offending vehicle did not have valid and SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2856/2024 effective driving license.

5. Vide order dated 01.08.2024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15.11.2023 at about 8.40 a.m., in front of Jyothi School, near Booragamakalahalli Village, on Srinivasapura - Chintamani road,
Chintamani Taluk, Chikkaballapura District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Maruthi Swift Dzire Car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-B-0326?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.2856/2024  3) What Order or Award?

 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2856/2024 driving of the driver of the Maruthi Swift Dzire car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-B-0326/offending vehicle.

In this regard the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 15.11.2023 he was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-JS-3267 towards Chintamani from his village Doddaganjuru as pillion rider, ridden by his friend slowly,
cautiously and on the way at about 8.45 a.m. when he reached in front of Jyothi School, near Booragamakalahalli, Srinivasapura - Chintamani road, Chintamani Taluk at that time the driver of the offending vehicle came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and went to its wrong side and dashed violently against the motorcycle of the petitioner, resulting in grievous injuries to the petitioner.

10. The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing of the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2856/2024 documents.
Ex.P1 is the FIR registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint given by one Ananda on 17.11.2023 as per Ex.P2.
As far as the delay in lodging the complaint is concerned it is stated that the petitioner was under treatment in the hospital and hence there is a delay in lodging the complaint.
Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar which discloses that the width of the accident road is about 25 feet with footpath on either side of the road and the spot of the accident is in front of Jyothi School.
Ex.P4 is the vehicle seizure mahazar.
Ex.P5 is the IMV report which discloses the damages sustained to the vehicles involved in the accident.
Ex.P6 is the wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner sustained injuries due to the impact of the accident.

Ex.P7 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC which discloses that the petitioner sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2856/2024 offending vehicle.
Hence, these documents produced by the petitioner satisfactorily establish that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination of PW.1, he has deposed that my friend was riding the motorcycle and denied that they were not wearing the helmet.
It is suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that he has colluded with the police and filed false complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner's side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2856/2024 withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.

The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offences under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence Bhavishath K A vs Naresha C R on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168679516/

SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2856/2024 12. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:
As far as the medical bills are concerned the petitioner has produced Ex.P6 - wound certificate.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P8 - discharge summary which discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Sri Gaurav Orthopedic &
Surgical hospital from 15.11.2023 to 18.11.2023.
Ex.P9 are the medical bills 11 in nos.
As far as the medical bills are concerned, except suggesting that the said bills are created, nothing is elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
Hence in view of Ex.P9 petitioner is awarded an amount of Rs.90,139/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P8 - discharge summary discloses that the petitioner has SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2856/2024 sustained left femur - fracture middle third femur shaft and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and petitioner cannot do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 20 years and he was doing agriculture and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In this regard PW.1 has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner it would be proper to assume the SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2856/2024 monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident.
As per the minimum wages chart and KALSA guidelines the notional income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m for assessing compensation.

Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 3 months hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,000 X 3 = 48,000/- under this head.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:

The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit he has permanent disability and as per the evidence of PW.2 his impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that he cannot pursue his work as before the accident.

sentences.text: In support of the same, PW.2 - Orthopaedic Surgeon is examined and he has deposed that the petitioner has sustained fracture middle third shaft of left femur - left leg and SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2856/2024 underwent surgery i.e., closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing for left femur and now he has complain of pain in the left hip and knee on doing strenuous activities and finds difficulty in climbing stairs, squatting, sit cross leg and kneeling and he assessed left lower limb disability of 42% and whole body is 14%.
PW.2 is cross
- examined by learned counsel for respondent No.2 and he has deposed that the fracture is united and implants can be removed and the petitioner can walk without any support.
It is admitted that he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability and denied that the disability is assessed on the higher side.
Taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner as far as functional disability is concerned the petitioner can do his work with some difficulties.
Hence it is just and proper to take the disability as 1/3 to the whole body which is already assessed at 14%.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.16,000/- at the relevant time.

As far as, age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2856/2024 perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P11 the birth year of the petitioner is 07.03.2004.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 15.11.2023 was around 19 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '18' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.

17. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2856/2024 disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
18. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he needs help of an attendant and conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.
19. COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:

It is stated in the evidence of PW.2 that Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of the implant and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.35,000/- to Bhavishath K A vs Naresha C R on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168679516/

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

20. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  48,000/-
up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  90,139/-
6. Loss of Future Income 4,83,840/-
7. Future medical expenses  20,000/-
Total 7,11,979/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 7,11,979/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 7,11,979/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E-payment and after proper identification.

The remaining 25%
award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
